12-1.title: Query rewriting vs expansion
12-1.tldr: Rewriting makes a query self-contained (coreference, typos, prior-turn reliance); expansion adds terms/synonyms or a hypothetical answer (HyDE) to bridge vocabulary gaps.
points: Rewriting: coreference/ellipsis, typos, drop turn dependence.
Expansion: synonyms or a hypothetical answer (HyDE).
Rewriting for multi-turn/malformed; expansion for vocabulary mismatch.

12-2.title: Handling vague queries
12-2.tldr: Detect ambiguity and either ask a clarifying question or rewrite to the most likely intent; cheap path is a rewrite, interactive path is a clarification turn.
points: Rewrite resolves coreference/ellipsis for free.
Ask a clarification only when it changes the retrieval target.
Don't blindly retrieve on an ambiguous query.

12-3.title: Decomposing multi-part questions
12-3.tldr: Split a compound question into independently answerable sub-questions, retrieve for each (often in parallel), then synthesize.
points: Break 'compare A and B on X and Y' into sub-questions.
Retrieve per sub-question; merge and dedupe.
Synthesize across the sub-answers.

12-4.title: Multi-hop retrieval
12-4.tldr: Multi-hop runs more than one retrieval step, using the first hop's result to form the next query, because the answer needs a bridging entity not present in the original question.
points: The answer needs a bridging entity/fact.
Each hop feeds the next query.
Single-pass fails when the link isn't in the query.

12-5.title: Multi-document questions
12-5.tldr: Retrieve a candidate set per sub-query or entity, merge and deduplicate, and let the generator synthesize across them (or add an aggregation step).
points: Per-sub-query retrieval, then merge/dedupe.
Ranked-list fusion across queries.
Generator synthesizes across documents.

12-6.title: When to skip RAG
12-6.tldr: Skip retrieval for general knowledge the model already holds, when latency/cost matter and the corpus won't add signal, or for conversational turns — but you need a way to decide.
points: Skip for general knowledge, reasoning, or code the model knows.
Skip when the corpus adds no signal and cost/latency matter.
Decide with a classifier or a sufficiency check.

12-7.title: How many retrieval hops
12-7.tldr: Use a sufficiency check to stop when evidence answers the question, and cap hops with a hard limit plus repetition and cost guards.
points: Stop when evidence is sufficient.
Hard hop cap as a backstop.
Repetition detection + cost ceiling.

12-8.title: Router pattern
12-8.tldr: One entry point decides which subsystem handles the request: the query is classified and routed to a specialized agent or tool.
points: Classify the query.
Route to a specialized handler.
Avoid one generic prompt.
